title.zh: 卷503 列傳二百九十 艺術二
title.raw: 卷503 列傳二百九十 艺術二

sentences.zh: 王澍蔣衡徐用錫王文治梁巘梁同書

translations.literal: Wang Shu, Jiang Heng, Xu Yongxi, Wang Wenzhi, Liang Yan, Liang Tongshu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu, Jiang Heng, Xu Yongxi, Wang Wenzhi, Liang Yan, and Liang Tongshu

sentences.zh: 鄧石如錢伯坰吳育楊沂孫吳熙載梅植之楊亮

translations.literal: Deng Shiru, Qian Bokan, Wu Yu, Yang Yisun, Wu Xizai, Mei Zhizhi, Yang Liang
translations.idiomatic: Deng Shiru, Qian Bokan, Wu Yu, Yang Yisun, Wu Xizai, Mei Zhizhi, and Yang Liang

sentences.zh: 王澍，字若林，號虛舟，江南金壇人。

translations.literal: Wang Shu, style name Ruolin, sobriquet Xuzhou, a man of Jintan in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu, whose courtesy name was Ruolin and sobriquet Xuzhou, came from Jintan in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 績學工文，尤以書名。

translations.literal: He accumulated learning and was skilled in letters, but was especially famous for calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply learned and accomplished as a writer, yet he was above all renowned for his calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十一年進士，入翰林，累遷戶科給事中。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year of Kangxi he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin, and was repeatedly promoted to supervising censor of the Household Branch.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifty-first year of the Kangxi reign, entered the Hanlin Academy, and rose in due course to supervising censor of the Household Branch.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，詔以六科隸都察院。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng, an edict placed the Six Offices under the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign, an imperial edict subordinated the Six Offices to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 澍謂科臣掌封駁，品卑任重，儻隸台臣，將廢科參，偕同官崔致遠、康五端抗疏力爭。

translations.literal: Shu said that Office censors were in charge of sealing and rebuttal, low in rank but heavy in responsibility; if they were subordinated to Censorate censors, Office memorials would be abandoned. Together with colleagues Cui Zhiyuan and Kang Wuduan he submitted a memorial firmly protesting.
translations.idiomatic: Shu argued that the Office censors handled sealing and rebuttal of memorials—low in rank yet weighty in duty—and that subordinating them to the Censorate would effectively abolish Office participation. He joined his colleagues Cui Zhiyuan and Kang Wuduan in a forceful joint memorial of protest.

sentences.zh: 世宗怒。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor was angry.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 立召詰之，從容奏對，上意稍解，遂改吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was immediately summoned and questioned; he answered calmly, the emperor's mind was somewhat eased, and he was then transferred to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him at once for interrogation; Shu answered with composure, the sovereign's anger eased somewhat, and he was reassigned as a vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 越二年，告歸，益耽書，名播海內。

translations.literal: After two years he requested leave to return home, devoted himself ever more to calligraphy, and his fame spread within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he retired to his home district, threw himself ever more deeply into calligraphy, and his reputation spread throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 摹古名搨殆遍，四體並工。

translations.literal: He copied famous ancient rubbings nearly to completion and was skilled in all four script forms.
translations.idiomatic: He traced nearly every celebrated ancient rubbing and mastered all four standard script forms.

sentences.zh: 於唐賢歐、褚兩家，致力尤深​​，輒跋尾自道所得。

translations.literal: Toward the Tang masters Ouyang and Chu he devoted himself especially deeply, and would append colophons stating what he had gained.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself above all to the Tang masters Ouyang Xun and Chu Suiliang, and habitually added colophons explaining what he had learned from each work.

sentences.zh: 後內閣學士翁方綱持論與異，謂其篆書得古法，行書次之，正書又次之。

translations.literal: Later Academician of the Grand Secretariat Weng Fanggang held a different view, saying his seal script obtained ancient methods, running script was next, and regular script ranked below again.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Academician of the Grand Secretariat Weng Fanggang took a different view, holding that Shu's seal script preserved the ancient manner, his running script came next, and his regular script ranked below both.

sentences.zh: 所著題跋及淳化閣帖考正，並行於世。

translations.literal: His colophons and Critical Study of the Chunhua Pavilion Rubbings both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His colophons and his Critical Study of the Chunhua Pavilion Rubbings both circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 自明、清之際，工書者，河北以王鐸、傅山為冠，繼則江左王鴻緒、姜宸英、何焯、汪士鋐、張照等，接踵而起，多見他傳。

translations.literal: From the Ming-Qing transition, among those skilled in calligraphy, north of the river Wang Duo and Fu Shan were foremost; then in the Jiangzuo region Wang Hongxu, Jiang Chenying, He Chao, Wang Shihong, Zhang Zhao, and others rose one after another—most are seen in other biographies.
translations.idiomatic: From the Ming-Qing transition onward, the leading calligraphers of Hebei were Wang Duo and Fu Shan; in the lower Yangtze region Wang Hongxu, Jiang Chenying, He Chao, Wang Shihong, Zhang Zhao, and others followed in quick succession—most of whom are treated in other biographies.

sentences.zh: 大抵淵源出於明文徵明、董其昌兩家，鴻緒、照為董氏嫡派，焯及澍則於文氏為近。

translations.literal: For the most part their sources came from the Ming masters Wen Zhengming and Dong Qichang; Hongxu and Zhao were direct heirs of the Dong school, while Chao and Shu were closer to the Wen school.
translations.idiomatic: Their lineages for the most part traced back to the Ming masters Wen Zhengming and Dong Qichang: Hongxu and Zhao were direct heirs of Dong Qichang's tradition, while He Chao and Wang Shu stood closer to Wen Zhengming's.

sentences.zh: 澍論書尤詳，一時所宗。

translations.literal: Shu's discussions of calligraphy were especially detailed and were honored by his age.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's writings on calligraphy were especially thorough, and his age looked to him as an authority.

sentences.zh: 蔣衡，改名振生，字湘帆，晚號拙老人。

translations.literal: Jiang Heng, who changed his name to Zhensheng, style name Xiangfan, late sobriquet Zhuolaoren.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Heng, who later changed his name to Zhensheng, had the courtesy name Xiangfan and in his later years took the sobriquet Zhuolaoren, 'the Clumsy Old Man.'

sentences.zh: 與澍同里。

translations.literal: He was from the same district as Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He came from the same home district as Wang Shu.

sentences.zh: 鍵戶十二年，寫十三經。

translations.literal: He barred his door for twelve years and wrote out the Thirteen Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He shut himself indoors for twelve years and copied out the entire Thirteen Classics in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，進上，高宗命刻石國學，授衡國子監學正，終不出。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong reign he presented it to the throne; the Gaozong Emperor ordered it carved in stone at the Imperial Academy and appointed Heng director of studies at the Directorate of Education, but he never took office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianlong reign he presented his work to the throne; the Qianlong Emperor ordered it cut in stone at the Imperial Academy and appointed Heng director of studies at the Directorate of Education, yet he never left home to serve.

sentences.zh: 衡早歲好遊，足跡半海內，觀碑關中，獲晉、唐以來名跡，臨摹三百餘種，曰拙存堂臨古帖。

translations.literal: Heng in his early years loved travel; his footsteps covered half the realm. Viewing steles in Guanzhong he obtained famous traces from Jin and Tang onward, copied more than three hundred kinds, and called them Zhuocuntang Copies of Ancient Rubbings.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Heng loved to travel and ranged over half the empire; in Guanzhong he studied steles and acquired celebrated works from the Jin and Tang dynasties onward, producing more than three hundred copies collected as the Zhuocuntang Copies of Ancient Rubbings.

sentences.zh: 晚與澍相期斫勝，每臨一書，相從質證。

translations.literal: In his later years he and Shu arranged to compare their skill; whenever either copied a work, the other would follow along to verify it.
translations.idiomatic: In later life he and Wang Shu made a practice of testing each other's skill: whenever one copied a classic work, the other would join him to critique and verify the result.

sentences.zh: 子驥，孫和，並以書世其家。

translations.literal: His son Ji and grandson He both handed down calligraphy through their family.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiang Ji and grandson Jiang He both carried on the family's reputation in calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 驥尤精分隸，著漢隸譌體集、古帖字體、續書法論各一卷，兼工畫。

translations.literal: Ji was especially skilled in clerical and official script, authored one juan each of Collected Errata in Han Clerical Script, Character Forms in Ancient Rubbings, and Continued Treatise on Calligraphy, and was also skilled in painting.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was especially accomplished in clerical and official script; he wrote one fascicle each of Collected Errata in Han Clerical Script, Character Forms in Ancient Rubbings, and Continued Treatise on Calligraphy, and was also an accomplished painter.

sentences.zh: 其言曰：「漢、魏字體不同，性情各異。

translations.literal: He said: 'The character forms of Han and Wei differ, and their temperaments are each distinct.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: 'The scripts of Han and Wei differ, and each bears a distinct temperament.

sentences.zh: 書須懸臂中鋒，而用力以和平為主。

translations.literal: In writing one must suspend the arm and use the central brush-tip, and in applying force take evenness and harmony as primary.
translations.idiomatic: Writing requires the suspended arm and a centered brush tip; force should above all be even and harmonious.

sentences.zh: 作畫之提頓逆折，參差映帶，其理一爾。」

translations.literal: The lifting, pausing, reversing, and folding in painting, and their staggered echoing and binding—the principle is one.'
translations.idiomatic: The lift, pause, counter-turn, and staggered echoing that govern painting follow the very same principle.'

sentences.zh: 皆闡明其先說。

translations.literal: —all elucidating his forebears' doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: These remarks all elaborate the doctrines of his forebears.

sentences.zh: 徐用錫，字壇長，宿遷人，佔籍大興。

translations.literal: Xu Yongxi, style name Tanchang, a man of Suqian, registered domicile in Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yongxi, courtesy name Tanchang, was a native of Suqian who registered his domicile in Daxing.

sentences.zh: 登鄉舉，康熙四十八年進士，官翰林院編修。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination, became a jinshi in the forty-eighth year of Kangxi, and served as compiler in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the provincial examination he took the jinshi degree in the forty-eighth year of Kangxi and served as a compiler in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 從李光地遊，究心樂律、音韻、歷數、書法。

translations.literal: He followed Li Guangdi and devoted himself to music theory, phonology, calendrical calculation, and calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Li Guangdi and devoted himself to music theory, phonology, calendrical science, and calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，分校會試，嚴絕請託，銜之者反嗾言官劾其把持闈事，聖祖原之，終以浮議罷歸。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he served as associate examiner for the metropolitan examination, strictly refusing requests and favors; those who resented him incited censors to impeach him for controlling examination affairs. The Shengzu Emperor forgave him, but in the end he was dismissed and returned home on account of loose talk.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year he served as an associate examiner for the metropolitan examination and refused patronage requests outright; his enemies stirred up censors to accuse him of manipulating the examination hall. Though the Kangxi Emperor excused him, he was eventually forced home by unsubstantiated gossip.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，起授翰林院侍讀，年已八十。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong he was recalled and appointed Hanlin reader, already eighty years old.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign he was recalled and appointed a Hanlin reader at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 尋告歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: Soon he requested leave to return and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired again and died at home.

sentences.zh: 用錫鄉舉出姜宸英之門，與何焯同為光地客，論書多與二家相出入。

translations.literal: Yongxi's provincial examination came from Jiang Chenying's school; he and He Chao were both guests of Li Guangdi, and his discussions of calligraphy largely agreed with, and at times diverged from, those two houses.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi had passed the provincial examination under Jiang Chenying; he and He Chao were both protégés of Li Guangdi, and his views on calligraphy largely aligned with, yet sometimes diverged from, those two masters.

sentences.zh: 精於鑑別古人，言筆法亦多心得，著字學劄記二卷，載圭美堂集中。

translations.literal: He was skilled in appraising ancient works; his remarks on brush method also contained many personal insights. He authored two juan of Notes on Character Studies, included in the Guimeitang Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He was an expert appraiser of ancient calligraphy and had many original insights on brush technique; his two-fascicle Notes on Character Studies is preserved in the Guimeitang Collection.

sentences.zh: 王文治，字禹卿，江蘇丹徒人。

translations.literal: Wang Wenzhi, style name Yuqing, a man of Dantu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenzhi, courtesy name Yuqing, was a native of Dantu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 生有夙慧，十二歲能詩，即工書。

translations.literal: Born with innate intelligence, at twelve he could compose poetry and was already skilled in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: He was gifted from childhood: at twelve he could write poetry and was already accomplished in calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 長游京師，從翰林院侍讀全魁使琉球，文字播於海外。

translations.literal: When grown he traveled to the capital; he followed Hanlin reader Quan Kui on a mission to Ryukyu, and his writing spread beyond the seas.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he traveled to the capital and accompanied the Hanlin reader Quan Kui on a mission to Ryukyu, where his writing won renown overseas.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十五年，成一甲三名進士，授翰林院編修。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Qianlong he placed third among the first-rank jinshi and was appointed Hanlin compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year of Qianlong he placed third in the first rank of jinshi graduates and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 逾三年，大考第一，擢侍讀。

translations.literal: After more than three years, in the grand examination he ranked first and was promoted to reader.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he ranked first in the grand examination and was promoted to Hanlin reader.

sentences.zh: 出為雲南臨安知府，因事鐫級，乞病歸。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Lin'an in Yunnan; because of an affair his rank was reduced, and he requested leave on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as prefect of Lin'an in Yunnan, but after an incident his rank was reduced; he pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 後當復官，厭吏事，遂不出，往來吳、越間，主講杭州、鎮江書院。

translations.literal: Later he was due to be restored to office, but he was weary of administrative affairs and so did not emerge; he traveled between Wu and Yue and lectured at academies in Hangzhou and Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: When he was later eligible for reinstatement he had grown weary of official business and declined to serve, traveling between the Wu and Yue regions while lecturing at academies in Hangzhou and Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 高宗南巡，至錢塘僧寺，見文治書碑，大賞愛之。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor made a southern tour and came to a Buddhist temple in Qiantang, he saw a stele inscribed by Wenzhi and greatly admired it.
translations.idiomatic: On a southern tour the Qianlong Emperor visited a Buddhist temple in Qiantang, saw a stele inscribed by Wenzhi, and was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 內廷有以告，招之出者，亦不應。

translations.literal: Someone in the inner court reported this; those who summoned him to come forth received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached the inner court, and although he was summoned to serve, he would not answer the call.

sentences.zh: 喜聲伎，行輒以歌伶一部自隨，辨論音律，窮極幽渺。

translations.literal: He delighted in music and entertainers; whenever he traveled he took a troupe of singers with him, and in discussing musical pitch he plumbed the most subtle and remote.
translations.idiomatic: He loved music and the theater and always traveled with a company of singers; in discussions of pitch and mode he explored the subtlest refinements.

sentences.zh: 客至張樂，窮朝暮不倦。

translations.literal: When guests arrived he would set out music and carry on from morning to evening without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: When guests arrived he would hold forth with music from dawn to dusk without tiring.

sentences.zh: 海內求書者，多有餽遺，率費於聲伎。

translations.literal: Those within the seas who sought his writing often presented gifts, which for the most part he spent on music and entertainers.
translations.idiomatic: Patrons from across the empire who sought his calligraphy often sent him gifts, nearly all of which he spent on music and performers.

sentences.zh: 然客散，默然禪定，夜坐，肋未嘗至席。

translations.literal: Yet when guests dispersed he would sit silently in Chan meditation through the night, his ribs never reaching the mat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once his guests had left he would sit in silent Chan meditation through the night, never letting his ribs touch the mat.

sentences.zh: 持佛戒，自言吾詩與書皆禪理也。

translations.literal: He kept Buddhist precepts and said of himself, 'My poetry and calligraphy are both Chan principles.'
translations.idiomatic: He observed the Buddhist precepts and declared, 'My poetry and my calligraphy are both expressions of Chan insight.'

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 所著詩集外有快雨堂題跋，略見論書之旨。

translations.literal: Besides his collected poems he had Kuaiyutang Colophons, which give a glimpse of his views on calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Besides his collected poems he left Kuaiyutang Colophons, which convey something of his views on calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 文治書名並時與劉墉相埒，人稱之曰「濃墨宰相，淡墨探花」。

translations.literal: Wenzhi's calligraphic fame in his time rivaled Liu Yong's; people called them 'the thick-ink Chancellor and the light-ink Flower of the Court.'
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhi's reputation in his day rivaled that of Liu Yong; people nicknamed them 'the thick-ink Chancellor and the light-ink Flower of the Court.'

sentences.zh: 與姚鼐交最深，論最契，當時書名，鼐不及文治之遠播；

translations.literal: He was closest in friendship and most in accord in discussion with Yao Nai; at that time in calligraphic fame Nai did not spread as far as Wenzhi;
translations.idiomatic: His closest friend and keenest intellectual companion was Yao Nai; at the time Yao's calligraphic fame did not travel as widely as Wenzhi's;

sentences.zh: 後包世臣極推鼐書，與劉墉並列上品，名轉出文治上。

translations.literal: later Bao Shichen greatly promoted Nai's writing, placing it with Liu Yong in the highest grade, and his fame in turn rose above Wenzhi's.
translations.idiomatic: later Bao Shichen championed Yao's calligraphy, ranking it with Liu Yong's among the finest, and Yao's reputation eventually eclipsed Wenzhi's.

sentences.zh: 梁巘，字聞山，安徽亳州人。

translations.literal: Liang Yan, style name Wenshan, a man of Bozhou in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yan, courtesy name Wenshan, was a native of Bozhou in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十七年舉人，官四川巴縣知縣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Qianlong he became a provincial graduate and served as magistrate of Baxian in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the twenty-seventh year of Qianlong and served as magistrate of Baxian in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 晚辭官，主講壽春書院，以工李北海書名於世。

translations.literal: In his later years he resigned office, lectured at the Shouchun Academy, and was famous in the world for skill in the style of Li Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: In later life he resigned his post, became head lecturer at the Shouchun Academy, and won fame for his mastery of the calligraphic manner of Li Yong of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 初為咸安宮教習，至京師，聞欽天監正何國宗曾以事系刑部，時尚書張照亦以他事在系，得其筆法，因詣家就問。

translations.literal: At first he was an instructor at the Xian'an Palace; when he reached the capital he heard that Director of the Astronomical Bureau He Guozong had once been detained in the Ministry of Justice over an affair, and that at the time Minister Zhang Zhao was also detained for another matter and had obtained his brush method—so he went to his home to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as an instructor at the Xian'an Palace; on reaching the capital he learned that the Director of the Astronomical Bureau He Guozong had once been held in the Ministry of Justice, and that the Minister Zhang Zhao had been detained at the same time and had learned He's brush technique—so Liang went to He's home to seek instruction.

sentences.zh: 國宗年已八十餘，病不能對客，遣一孫傳語。

translations.literal: Guozong was already over eighty, ill and unable to receive guests, and sent a grandson to convey his words.
translations.idiomatic: Guozong was already over eighty, too ill to receive visitors, and sent a grandson to speak for him.

sentences.zh: 巘質以所聞，國宗答曰：「君已得之矣。」

translations.literal: Yan questioned him about what he had heard; Guozong answered: 'You have already obtained it.'
translations.idiomatic: Liang questioned him about what he had learned; Guozong replied, 'You have already grasped it.'

sentences.zh: 贈以所臨米、黃二帖。

translations.literal: He presented him with his copies of the Mi and Huang rubbings.
translations.idiomatic: He then presented him with his own copies of works after Mi Fu and Huang Tingjian.

sentences.zh: 後巘以語金壇段玉裁曰：「執筆之法，指以運臂，臂以運身。

translations.literal: Later Yan told Duan Yucai of Jintan: 'The method of holding the brush: the fingers move the arm, and the arm moves the body.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liang told Duan Yucai of Jintan: 'In holding the brush, the fingers set the arm in motion, and the arm sets the whole body in motion.

sentences.zh: 凡捉筆，以大指尖與食指尖相對，筆正直在兩指尖之間，兩指尖相接如環，兩指本以上平，可安酒杯。

translations.literal: Whenever one grasps the brush, the tips of the thumb and forefinger face each other, the brush standing straight between the two finger-tips; the two tips meet like a ring, and from the bases of the two fingers upward is level, so that a wine cup could be set there.
translations.idiomatic: When you grasp the brush, set the tip of the thumb against the tip of the forefinger with the brush shaft upright between them; the two tips should meet like a ring, and from the knuckles upward the hand should be level enough to balance a wine cup.

sentences.zh: 平其肘，腕不附幾，肘圓而兩指與筆正當胸，令全身之力，行於臂而湊於兩指尖。

translations.literal: Level the elbow, the wrist not resting on the table; the elbow rounded and the two fingers and brush directly before the chest, causing the force of the whole body to travel through the arm and gather at the two finger-tips.
translations.idiomatic: Keep the elbow level and the wrist off the desk; with the elbow rounded and the two fingers and brush aligned before the chest, the body's full strength should pass through the arm and concentrate at the two fingertips.

sentences.zh: 兩指尖不圓如環，或如環而不平，則捉之也不緊，臂之力尚不能出，而況於身？

translations.literal: If the two finger-tips do not form a ring, or form a ring but are not level, then the grasp is not tight—the arm's force cannot yet emerge, how much less the body's?
translations.idiomatic: If the fingertips do not form a true ring, or form a ring but are not level, the grip is not tight—the arm's force cannot be released, much less the body's.

sentences.zh: 緊則身之力全湊於指尖，而何有於臂？

translations.literal: When tight, the body's force entirely gathers at the finger-tips—what need is there for the arm?
translations.idiomatic: When the grip is tight, the body's entire force gathers at the fingertips—what role remains for the arm alone?

sentences.zh: 古人知指之不能運臂也，故使指頂相接以固筆，筆管可斷，指鍥痛不可勝，而後字中有力。

translations.literal: The ancients knew that the fingers alone cannot move the arm, so they made the finger-tips meet to fix the brush—the brush shaft might break, but the fingers' wedged pain could not be borne, and only then did strength appear in the characters.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients knew the fingers cannot move the arm by themselves, so they joined the finger-tips to secure the brush—the shaft might snap, but the fingers' gripping pain was unbearable, and only then did the characters gain true force.

sentences.zh: 其以大指與食指也，謂之單勾；

translations.literal: Using the thumb and forefinger is called the single hook;
translations.idiomatic: Using the thumb and forefinger alone is called the single hook;

sentences.zh: 其以大指與食指中指也，謂之雙勾；

translations.literal: using the thumb with forefinger and middle finger is called the double hook;
translations.idiomatic: using the thumb with forefinger and middle finger is called the double hook;

sentences.zh: 中指者，所以輔食指之力也，總謂之'撥鐙法'。

translations.literal: the middle finger assists the forefinger's force—all together called the 'stirrup-pressing method.'
translations.idiomatic: the middle finger assists the forefinger's force—the whole technique is called the stirrup-pressing method.

sentences.zh: 王獻之七、八歲時學書，右軍從旁掣其筆不得，即謂此法。

translations.literal: When Wang Xianzhi was seven or eight and learning to write, the Right General tried to pull the brush from the side and could not—this is that method.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xianzhi was seven or eight and learning calligraphy, Wang Xizhi tried to pull the brush away from beside him and could not—this is that very method.

sentences.zh: 捨此法，皆旁門外道。

translations.literal: Abandon this method and all are heterodox bypaths.
translations.idiomatic: Abandon this method and every other way is a heterodox bypath.

sentences.zh: 二王以後，至唐、宋、元、明諸大家，口口相傳如是，董宗伯以授王司農鴻緒，司農以授張文敏，吾聞而知之。

translations.literal: After the Two Wangs, down to the great masters of Tang, Song, Yuan, and Ming, mouth to mouth it was transmitted thus: Master Dong gave it to Minister of Agriculture Wang Hongxu, the Minister of Agriculture gave it to Zhang Wenmin, and I heard and knew it.
translations.idiomatic: From the Two Wangs down through the great masters of Tang, Song, Yuan, and Ming it was handed down mouth to mouth in just this way: Dong Qichang taught Wang Hongxu, Wang Hongxu taught Zhang Zhao, and I learned it by hearing it passed on.

sentences.zh: 本朝但有一張文敏耳，他未為善。

translations.literal: In our dynasty there is only one Zhang Wenmin; the rest have not done well.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty there has been only one Zhang Zhao; no one else has mastered it properly.

sentences.zh: 王虛舟用筆祗得一半，蔣湘帆知握筆而少作字樂趣。

translations.literal: Wang Xuzhou in using the brush obtains only half; Jiang Xiangfan knows how to hold the brush but has little joy in making characters.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu has mastered only half of this brush method; Jiang Heng knows how to hold the brush but takes little pleasure in writing.

sentences.zh: 世人但言無火氣，不知火氣使盡，而後可言無火氣也。

translations.literal: People in the world only speak of having no fiery vigor, not knowing that only after fiery vigor is exhausted can one speak of having none.
translations.idiomatic: People talk only of doing away with fiery vigor, not realizing that one can speak of being free of it only after that vigor has been fully spent.

sentences.zh: 如此捉筆，則筆心不偏，中心透紙，紙上颯颯有聲。

translations.literal: Hold the brush thus and the brush-heart is not off-center; the center penetrates the paper, and on the paper there is a rustling sound.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the brush in this way and the brush core stays true; the center penetrates the paper, and the paper rustles audibly under the stroke.

sentences.zh: 直畫粗者濃墨兩分，中如有絲界，筆心為之主也。

translations.literal: In thick vertical strokes with heavy ink in two parts, in the middle there is like a silk boundary—the brush-heart is master.
translations.idiomatic: In a thick vertical stroke the ink may divide into two dark bands with a fine line between them like a silk thread—the brush core governs that effect.

sentences.zh: 如此捉筆，則必堅紙作字，輭薄紙當之易破。

translations.literal: Hold the brush thus and one must write on firm paper; soft thin paper offered to it is easily torn.
translations.idiomatic: With this grip one must write on stiff paper; soft, thin paper will tear under the pressure.

sentences.zh: 其橫、直、撇、捺皆與今人殊，筆鋒所指，方向迥異，筆心總在每筆之中，無少偏也。

translations.literal: Its horizontal, vertical, slanting, and pressing strokes are all unlike those of people today; the direction the brush-tip points is utterly different, and the brush-heart is always in the middle of each stroke, without the slightest deviation.
translations.idiomatic: Its horizontals, verticals, slants, and presses all differ from modern practice; the brush tip points in wholly different directions, and the brush core always stays at the center of each stroke without the slightest deviation.

sentences.zh: 古人所謂屋漏痕、折釵股、錐畫沙、印印泥者，於此可悟入。」

translations.literal: What the ancients called 'roof-leak traces,' 'folded hairpin shanks,' 'awl drawing on sand,' and 'seal pressing into mud'—through this one may enter into understanding.'
translations.idiomatic: The ancient metaphors of roof-leak traces, folded hairpin shanks, awl marks in sand, and a seal pressed into mud can all be understood through this practice.'

sentences.zh: 巘少著述，所傳緒論僅此。

translations.literal: Yan wrote little; the transmitted threads of theory are only this.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yan wrote little; this is virtually all that survives of his transmitted theory.

sentences.zh: 當時與梁同書並稱，巘曰「北梁」，同書曰「南梁」。

translations.literal: At the time he and Liang Tongshu were spoken of together: Yan was called 'Northern Liang,' Tongshu 'Southern Liang.'
translations.idiomatic: In his day he and Liang Tongshu were paired in fame: Yan was called 'Northern Liang' and Tongshu 'Southern Liang.'

sentences.zh: 梁同書，字元穎，晚號山舟，浙江錢塘人，大學士詩正子。

translations.literal: Liang Tongshu, style name Yuanying, late sobriquet Shanzhou, a man of Qiantang in Zhejiang, son of Grand Secretary Shizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Tongshu, courtesy name Yuanying, who in later life took the sobriquet Shanzhou, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang and the son of the Grand Secretary Liang Shizheng.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十七年，會試未第，高宗特賜與殿試，入翰林，大考，擢侍講。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Qianlong he failed the metropolitan examination; the Gaozong Emperor specially granted him participation in the palace examination. He entered the Hanlin, and in the grand examination was promoted to expositor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Qianlong he failed the metropolitan examination, but the Qianlong Emperor specially allowed him to take the palace examination; he entered the Hanlin Academy and, after the grand examination, was promoted to expositor.

sentences.zh: 淡於榮利，未老，因疾不出。

translations.literal: Indifferent to glory and profit, before he was old he ceased to emerge on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Indifferent to rank and gain, he withdrew from office while still comparatively young, pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 晚年重宴鹿鳴，加侍講學士銜。

translations.literal: In his later years he was again feasted at the Luming banquet and given the additional title of expositor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he was again honored at the Luming banquet for senior graduates and granted the additional title of Hanlin expositor.

sentences.zh: 卒，年九十三。

translations.literal: He died at the age of ninety-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of ninety-three.

sentences.zh: 好書出天性，十二歲能為擘窠大字。

translations.literal: His love of calligraphy came from innate nature; at twelve he could write large characters in boke style.
translations.idiomatic: His love of calligraphy was inborn; at twelve he could write large decorative characters.

sentences.zh: 初法顏、柳，中年用米法，七十後乃變化。

translations.literal: At first he followed Yan and Liu; in middle age he used Mi's method; only after seventy did he transform.
translations.idiomatic: He began by studying Yan Zhenqing and Liu Gongquan; in midlife he adopted Mi Fu's manner; only after seventy did his style fully mature into something his own.

sentences.zh: 名滿天下，求書者紙日數束，日本、琉球皆重之。

translations.literal: His fame filled the world; those who sought his writing sent several bundles of paper daily; Japan and Ryukyu all prized him.
translations.idiomatic: His fame filled the world; patrons sent him several bundles of paper each day seeking his writing, and collectors in Japan and Ryukyu prized his work highly.

sentences.zh: 嘗與張燕昌論書，略曰：「古人云『筆力直透紙背』，當與天馬行空參看。

translations.literal: He once discussed calligraphy with Zhang Yanchang, saying in brief: 'The ancients said "brush force penetrates straight through the paper's back"—this should be considered together with "heavenly horses roaming the void.
translations.idiomatic: He once discussed calligraphy with Zhang Yanchang and remarked in part: 'The ancients said that brush force penetrates straight through the back of the paper—this should be read together with the image of heavenly horses roaming free.

sentences.zh: 今人誤認透紙，便如藥山所云『看穿牛皮』，終無是處。

translations.literal: People today mistakenly take penetrating the paper to mean, as Yaoshan said, 'seeing through ox-hide'—there is ultimately no point in that.
translations.idiomatic: People today mistake penetrating the paper for what Master Yaoshan called 'seeing through ox-hide'—a notion that leads nowhere.

sentences.zh: 蓋透紙者，狀其精氣結撰墨光浮溢耳，彼用筆如游絲者，何嘗不透紙背耶？

translations.literal: For penetrating the paper describes how vital essence gathers and ink-light overflows; those who use the brush like gossamer—how have they failed to penetrate the paper's back?
translations.idiomatic: Penetrating the paper describes how vital spirit gathers and ink-light seems to overflow the surface; those who wield the brush like gossamer—have they not also penetrated the back of the paper?

sentences.zh: 用腕力使極輭之筆自見，譬如人持一彊者，使之直，則無所用力；

translations.literal: Use wrist force and an extremely soft brush reveals itself; it is like a person holding something stiff—if he makes it straight, he has nowhere to apply force;
translations.idiomatic: Wrist force makes an extremely soft brush effective on its own; it is like holding something stiff—if you try to keep it straight, you have nowhere to apply force;

sentences.zh: 持一弱者，慾不使之偃，則全腕之力，自然集於兩指端。

translations.literal: hold something weak and, wishing not to let it bend, the whole wrist's force naturally gathers at the two finger-tips.
translations.idiomatic: but hold something weak and, because you do not want it to bend, the full force of the wrist naturally gathers at the two fingertips.

sentences.zh: 其實書者只知指運，而不知有腕力也。

translations.literal: In truth calligraphers only know finger movement and do not know there is wrist force.
translations.idiomatic: In truth most calligraphers know only how the fingers move and are unaware of the wrist's role.

sentences.zh: 藏鋒之說，非筆如鈍錐之謂，自來書家從無不出鋒者，只是處處留得筆住，不使直走。

translations.literal: The doctrine of hidden tip does not mean the brush is like a blunt awl; from antiquity calligraphers have never failed to bring out the tip—they only everywhere keep the brush dwelling, not letting it run straight.
translations.idiomatic: The doctrine of hidden tip does not mean writing with a blunt awl; calligraphers have never failed to bring out the tip—they simply keep the brush dwelling at every turn rather than letting it run straight through.

sentences.zh: 筆耍輭，輭則遒；

translations.literal: The brush must be soft; when soft it is forceful;
translations.idiomatic: The brush should be supple; suppleness yields vigor;

sentences.zh: 筆要長，長則靈；

translations.literal: the brush must be long; when long it is spirited;
translations.idiomatic: it should be long; length gives life;

sentences.zh: 筆耍飽，飽則腴；

translations.literal: the brush must be full; when full it is plump;
translations.idiomatic: it must be well loaded with ink; fullness gives richness;

sentences.zh: 落筆耍快，快則意出。

translations.literal: the stroke must fall quickly; when quick, meaning emerges.
translations.idiomatic: the stroke must fall swiftly; speed brings the idea forth.

sentences.zh: 書家燥鋒曰渴筆，畫家亦有枯筆，二字判然不同。

translations.literal: Calligraphers call a dry tip a 'thirsty brush'; painters also have a 'withered brush'—the two terms are clearly different.
translations.idiomatic: Calligraphers speak of a 'thirsty brush' when the tip runs dry; painters also speak of a 'withered brush'—the two terms are by no means the same.

sentences.zh: 渴則不潤，枯則死矣。

translations.literal: Thirsty is not moist; withered is dead.
translations.idiomatic: Thirst means lack of moisture; withering means lifelessness.

sentences.zh: ​​今人喜用硬筆故枯。

translations.literal: People today like to use hard brushes and so their work is withered.
translations.idiomatic: People today favor hard brushes, and that is why their writing looks lifeless.

sentences.zh: 帖教人看，不教人摹。

translations.literal: Rubbings teach one to look, not to copy.
translations.idiomatic: Model books are meant to be studied with the eye, not traced like exercises.

sentences.zh: 今人只是刻舟求劍，將古人書摹畫如小兒寫仿本，就便形似，豈復有我？

translations.literal: People today merely mark the boat to seek the sword, copying ancient writing like children writing imitation books—though the form may resemble, how can there still be a self?
translations.idiomatic: People today merely chase fixed forms, copying ancient masters like schoolchildren tracing models; even when the likeness is there, where is the writer's own presence?

sentences.zh: 字耍有氣，氣須從熟得來。

translations.literal: Characters must have breath; breath must come from mastery.
translations.idiomatic: Writing must have breath and spirit, and that spirit can come only from long practice.

sentences.zh: 有氣則有勢，大小、長短、高下、欹整，隨筆所至，自然貫注，成一片段，卻著不得絲毫擺佈，熟後自知。

translations.literal: With breath there is momentum; large and small, long and short, high and low, leaning and straight—wherever the brush goes, it naturally flows through, forming a single passage, yet not admitting the slightest contrivance; after mastery one knows this oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Where there is breath there is momentum: size, length, height, tilt, and alignment follow the brush naturally and cohere into a single passage, yet not the slightest artificial arrangement is allowed—only after long practice does one understand this for oneself.

sentences.zh: 中鋒之法，筆提得起，自然中，亦未嘗無兼用側鋒處，總為我一縷筆尖所使，雖不中亦中。

translations.literal: The method of the centered tip: when the brush can be lifted, it is naturally centered; there are also places where the side tip is used together—altogether governed by my single thread of brush-tip; though not centered, it is still centered.
translations.idiomatic: In the centered-tip method, if the brush can be lifted freely it is naturally centered; there are also moments when the side of the tip is used, yet all are governed by a single thread of intention at the brush point—even when not literally centered, it is centered in effect.

sentences.zh: 亂頭粗服非字也，求逸則野，求舊則拙，此處不可有半點名心在。」

translations.literal: Disheveled hair and coarse dress are not writing; seeking ease becomes rustic, seeking antiquity becomes clumsy—here one must not have the slightest thought of fame.'
translations.idiomatic: Sloppy, unkempt strokes are not true writing; pursue ease and you become rustic, pursue antiquity and you become clumsy—at this level not the slightest craving for reputation should remain.'

sentences.zh: 同書平生書旨，與梁巘之異同，具見於此。

translations.literal: Tongshu's lifelong principles of calligraphy, and his agreements and differences with Liang Yan, are all seen in this.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Tongshu's lifelong views on calligraphy, and how they agreed with or differed from Liang Yan's, are fully visible here.

sentences.zh: 鄧石如，初名避仁宗諱，遂以字行，改字頑伯，安徽懷寧人。

translations.literal: Deng Shiru, whose original given name conflicted with Emperor Renzong's (the Jiaqing Emperor's) personal-name taboo and who therefore went by his courtesy name, later changed his courtesy name to Wanbo; he was a man of Huaining in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Shiru, whose original given name violated the Jiaqing Emperor's taboo and who therefore went by his style name, later took the style Wanbo; he came from Huaining in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 居皖公山下，又號完白山人。

translations.literal: He lived beneath Mount Wan Gong and also styled himself the Hermit of Mount Wanbai.
translations.idiomatic: He lived beneath Mount Wan Gong and also took the sobriquet Hermit of Mount Wanbai.

sentences.zh: 少產僻鄉，鮮聞見，獨好刻石，仿漢人印篆甚工。

translations.literal: Born young in a remote district with little to hear or see, he alone loved carving stone and was very skilled in imitating Han seal script for seals.
translations.idiomatic: Raised in an isolated countryside with little exposure to the world, he devoted himself to stone carving and became highly skilled at imitating Han seal script for seals.

sentences.zh: 弱冠孤貧，遊壽州，梁巘見其篆書，驚為筆勢渾鷙，而未盡得古法。

translations.literal: At twenty he was orphaned and poor; traveling to Shouzhou, Liang Yan saw his seal script and was startled by its vigorous, fierce brush momentum, yet felt he had not fully obtained ancient methods.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor by twenty, he traveled to Shouzhou; Liang Yan saw his seal script and marveled at its bold, fierce brushwork, though he felt Deng had not yet fully mastered the ancient manner.

sentences.zh: 介謁江寧梅鏐，都御史成子也。

translations.literal: He was introduced to Mei Liu of Jiangning, son of the Censor-in-chief Mei Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was introduced to Mei Liu of Jiangning, son of the Censor-in-chief Mei Cheng.

sentences.zh: 家多L3藏金石善本，盡出示之，為具衣食楮墨，使專肄習。

translations.literal: The household had many fine collections of bronze and stone rubbings; all were shown him, and food, clothing, paper, and ink were provided so that he might devote himself wholly to study.
translations.idiomatic: The Mei household owned many fine bronze and stone rubbings; Mei showed him the entire collection, supplied his food, clothing, paper, and ink, and had him devote himself entirely to practice.

sentences.zh: 好石鼓文，李斯嶧山碑、泰山刻石，漢開母石闕，燉煌太守碑，吳蘇建國山碑，皇像天發神讖碑，唐李陽冰城隍廟碑、三墳記，每種臨摹各百本。

translations.literal: He loved the Stone Drum Inscriptions, Li Si's Mount Yi stele and Mount Tai inscription, the Han Kaimu stone que, the Dunhuang prefect stele, Wu Su Jian's Guoshan stele, the Huangxiang Tianfa Shenchen stele, and Tang Li Yangbing's City God Temple stele and Record of the Three Tombs—of each kind he made a hundred copies.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Stone Drum Inscriptions, Li Si's Mount Yi and Mount Tai inscriptions, the Han Kaimu stone que, the Dunhuang prefect stele, Wu Su Jian's Guoshan stele, Huang Xiang's Tianfa Shenchen stele, and Tang Li Yangbing's City God Temple stele and Record of the Three Tombs—making a hundred copies of each.

sentences.zh: 又苦篆體不備，寫說文解字二十本。

translations.literal: He also grieved that seal forms were incomplete and wrote out twenty copies of the Shuowen Jiezi.
translations.idiomatic: Finding seal forms still incomplete, he copied out the Shuowen Jiezi twenty times.

sentences.zh: 帝搜三代鐘鼎，秦、漢瓦當、碑額。

translations.literal: The emperor searched out bells and tripods of the Three Dynasties and Qin-Han tile-ends and stele crowns.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor was then gathering bells and tripods of the Three Dynasties along with Qin and Han tile-ends and stele crowns.

sentences.zh: 五年，篆書成。

translations.literal: After five years his seal script was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: After five years he had mastered seal script.

sentences.zh: 乃學漢分，臨史晨前、後碑，華山碑，白石神君，張遷，潘校官，孔羨，受禪，大饗諸碑，各五十本。

translations.literal: He then studied Han clerical script, copying the front and back Shi Chen steles, the Mount Hua stele, the White Stone Spirit Lord, Zhang Qian, Pan the Commandant, Kong Xian, the Accession to the Throne, the Grand Sacrifice, and other steles—fifty copies of each.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned to Han clerical script, copying the front and back Shi Chen steles, the Mount Hua stele, the White Stone Spirit Lord, Zhang Qian, Pan the Commandant, Kong Xian, the Accession to the Throne, the Grand Sacrifice, and other classics—fifty copies apiece.

sentences.zh: 三年，分書成。

translations.literal: After three years his clerical script was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he had mastered clerical script.

sentences.zh: 石如篆法以二李為宗，縱橫闢闔，得之史籀，稍參隸意，殺鋒以取勁折，字體微方，與秦、漢當額為近。

translations.literal: Shiru's seal method took the two Lis as patriarchs; in breadth and expansion he obtained it from Shi Zhou, with slight clerical influence; he cut the tip to gain forceful turns; the character forms were slightly square, close to Qin and Han stele crowns.
translations.idiomatic: Shiru's seal script took the two Li masters as its models; in its sweeping expansiveness it drew on Shi Zhou, with a touch of clerical influence; he pared the brush tip to achieve sharp turns, and his forms were slightly square, close to Qin and Han stele crowns.

sentences.zh: 分書結體嚴重，約嶧山、國山之法而為之。

translations.literal: His clerical script's structure was grave and solemn, roughly following the methods of Mount Yi and Mount Guo.
translations.idiomatic: His clerical script was grave in structure, broadly following the manners of the Mount Yi and Mount Guo inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 自謂：「吾篆未及陽冰，而分不減梁鵠。」

translations.literal: He said of himself: 'My seal script has not reached Yangbing, but my clerical script is not inferior to Liang He.'
translations.idiomatic: He said of himself, 'My seal script has not yet matched Li Yangbing, but my clerical script is no worse than Liang He's.'

sentences.zh: 客梅氏八年，學既成，遍遊名山水，以書刻自給。

translations.literal: He was a guest of the Mei family for eight years; when his learning was complete he traveled famous mountains and rivers everywhere, supporting himself by writing and carving.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years with the Mei family he completed his training, traveled famous landscapes throughout the empire, and supported himself by calligraphy and seal carving.

sentences.zh: 遊黃山，至歙，鬻篆於賈肆。

translations.literal: Traveling to Mount Huang, he reached She and sold seal script in shops.
translations.idiomatic: On a journey to Mount Huang he reached She county and sold seal-script works in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 編修張惠言故深究秦篆，時館修撰金榜家，偶見石如書，語榜曰：「今日得見上蔡真跡。」

translations.literal: Compiler Zhang Huiyan had long studied Qin seal script deeply; he was then staying at Compiler Jin Bang's home and chanced to see Shiru's writing, saying to Bang: 'Today I have seen the true traces of Shang Cai.'
translations.idiomatic: The compiler Zhang Huiyan was a deep student of Qin seal script; staying at the home of the compiler Jin Bang, he chanced upon Shiru's writing and told Jin, 'Today I have seen the authentic manner of Li Si of Shang Cai.'

sentences.zh: 乃冒雨同訪於荒寺，榜備禮客之於家。

translations.literal: They then braved rain together to visit him at a deserted temple; Bang prepared full rites and received him as a guest at home.
translations.idiomatic: They braved the rain to visit him at a deserted temple, and Jin Bang received him at home with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 薦於尚書曹文埴，偕至京師，大學士劉墉、副都御史陸錫熊皆驚異曰：「千數百年無此作矣！」

translations.literal: He was recommended to Minister Cao Wenzhuan and went with him to the capital; Grand Secretary Liu Yong and Vice Censor-in-chief Lu Xixiong were both startled and said: 'For a thousand years there has been nothing like this!'
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended to the Minister Cao Wenzhuan and accompanied him to the capital; the Grand Secretary Liu Yong and the Vice Censor-in-chief Lu Xixiong both exclaimed in wonder, 'For a thousand years there has been nothing like this work!'

sentences.zh: 時京師論篆、分者，多宗內閣學士翁方綱，方綱以石如不至其門，力詆之。

translations.literal: At the time those in the capital who discussed seal and clerical script mostly followed Grand Secretary Weng Fanggang; Fanggang, because Shiru did not come to his door, denounced him forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: At the time most Beijing critics of seal and clerical script followed the Grand Secretary Weng Fanggang, who attacked Shiru fiercely because he had not paid court to him.

sentences.zh: 石如乃去，客兩湖總督畢沅，沅故好客，吳中名士多集節署，裘馬都麗，石如獨布衣徒步。

translations.literal: Shiru then left and became a guest of the Huguang governor Bi Yuan; Yuan was fond of entertaining guests, and many famous men of Wu gathered at his headquarters in splendid fur and horse trappings, while Shiru alone wore plain cloth and walked on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Shiru then left for the Huguang governor Bi Yuan, a renowned host at whose headquarters Wu literati gathered in splendid style while Shiru alone went in plain dress on foot.

sentences.zh: 居三年，辭歸，沅為置田宅，俾終老。

translations.literal: After three years he requested leave to return; Yuan set up fields and a house for him so that he might end his days in peace.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he took his leave; Bi Yuan provided him with land and a house so that he could live out his old age in comfort.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，觴之，曰：「山人，吾幕府一服清涼散也！」

translations.literal: On the eve of departure he offered him wine and said: 'Hermit, you are one dose of cooling powder for my staff!'
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to leave, Bi offered him wine and said, 'Hermit, you are a single dose of cooling medicine for my entire staff!'

sentences.zh: 石如年四十六始娶，常往來江、淮間，卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: Shiru married only at forty-six, often traveled between the Yangtze and Huai, and died at sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Shiru did not marry until he was forty-six; he traveled frequently between the Yangtze and Huai regions and died at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 子傳密，初名廷璽，字守之。

translations.literal: His son Chuanmi, original name Tingxi, style name Shouzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Deng Chuanmi, originally named Tingxi, had the courtesy name Shouzhi.

sentences.zh: 從李兆洛學，晚客曾國籓幕。

translations.literal: He studied under Li Zhaoluo and in his later years was a guest in Zeng Guofan's staff.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Li Zhaoluo and in later life served as a guest in Zeng Guofan's secretariat.

sentences.zh: 能以篆書世其家。

translations.literal: He was able to hand down seal script through the family.
translations.idiomatic: He carried on the family's reputation in seal script.

sentences.zh: 當乾、嘉之間，嘉定錢坫、陽湖錢伯坰，皆以書名。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong and Jiaqing reigns, Qian Dian of Jiading and Qian Bokan of Yanghu were both famous for calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianlong and Jiaqing reigns, Qian Dian of Jiading and Qian Bokan of Yanghu were both renowned for calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 坫自負其篆直接陽冰，嘗遊焦山，見壁間篆書心經，嘆為陽冰之亞。

translations.literal: Dian prided himself that his seal script descended directly from Yangbing; once traveling to Mount Jiao he saw the Heart Sutra in seal script on a wall and sighed that it was second only to Yangbing.
translations.idiomatic: Dian prided himself on a seal script that descended directly from Li Yangbing; visiting Mount Jiao he saw a wall inscription of the Heart Sutra in seal script and declared it second only to Yangbing's own work.

sentences.zh: 既而知為石如所作，摭其不合六書者以為詆。

translations.literal: When he learned it was Shiru's work, he picked out places not conforming to the Six Scripts to use as slander.
translations.idiomatic: Learning it was Shiru's work, he collected instances that violated the Six Scripts to use as grounds for attack.

sentences.zh: 伯坰故服石如篆、分為絕業，及見其行、草，歎曰：「此楊少師神境也！」

translations.literal: Bokan had admired Shiru's seal and clerical script as supreme craft; when he saw his running and cursive script he sighed: 'This is the divine realm of Yang Shaoshi!'
translations.idiomatic: Bokan had long admired Shiru's seal and clerical script as supreme achievements; when he saw his running and cursive hand he exclaimed, 'This is the divine realm of Yang Ningshi!'

sentences.zh: 復與論筆法不合，遂助坫詆之尤力。

translations.literal: But when they again discussed brush method and disagreed, he then helped Dian slander him all the more forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when they debated brush technique and fell out, he joined Dian in attacking Shiru with redoubled vigor.

sentences.zh: 坫見儒林傳。

translations.literal: Dian is seen in the Biographies of Confucian Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Dian has his own entry in the Biographies of Confucian Scholars.

sentences.zh: 伯坰，字魯斯，自號僕射山人，尚書維城從子。

translations.literal: Bokan, style name Lusi, self-styled the Hermit of Pushe, nephew of Minister Weicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Bokan, courtesy name Lusi, who styled himself the Hermit of Pushe, was a nephew of the Minister Qian Weicheng.

sentences.zh: 少孤，力學，工詩嗜酒，廣交遊，以國子監生終。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he studied hard, was skilled in poetry and fond of wine, had wide friendships, and ended as a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he studied diligently, wrote fine poetry, loved wine, cultivated a wide circle of friends, and ended his days as a student of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 書學顏平原、李北海，嘗曰：「古人用兔毫，故書有中線，今用羊毫，其精者乃成雙鉤。

translations.literal: In calligraphy he studied Yan Pingyuan and Li Beihai, and once said: 'The ancients used rabbit hair, so writing had a central line; today we use goat hair, and only the finest achieves the double hook.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the manners of Yan Zhenqing and Li Yong of Beihai and once remarked, 'The ancients used rabbit-hair brushes, so their writing showed a central line; today we use goat hair, and only the finest work achieves the double hook.

sentences.zh: 吾躭此五十年，才十得三四。」

translations.literal: I have devoted myself to this for fifty years and have achieved only three or four parts in ten.'
translations.idiomatic: I have pursued this for fifty years and have mastered only three or four parts in ten.'

sentences.zh: 論者謂自劉墉歿，正、行書以伯坰為第一。

translations.literal: Critics said that since Liu Yong's death, in regular and running script Bokan ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Critics held that after Liu Yong's death, Bokan ranked first in regular and running script.

sentences.zh: 其執筆，虛小指，以三指包管外，與大指相拒，側毫入紙，助怒張之勢。

translations.literal: In holding the brush he left the little finger free, wrapped the shaft outside with three fingers opposing the thumb, entered the paper with the side of the tip, and aided the momentum of angry expansion.
translations.idiomatic: He held the brush with the little finger free, wrapped three fingers around the shaft against the thumb, entered the paper with the side of the tip, and thereby reinforced a bold, expansive stroke.

sentences.zh: 指腕皆不動，以肘來去，斥古今相承撥鐙之說。

translations.literal: Fingers and wrist did not move; he used the elbow to go back and forth, and rejected the stirrup-pressing doctrine handed down from antiquity to the present.
translations.idiomatic: His fingers and wrist did not move; he used the elbow alone, and rejected the stirrup-pressing doctrine handed down through the ages.

sentences.zh: 石如作書，則懸腕雙鉤，管隨指轉，兩家法大殊。

translations.literal: When Shiru wrote he suspended the wrist and used the double hook, the shaft turning with the fingers—the methods of the two houses were greatly different.
translations.idiomatic: Shiru wrote with suspended wrist and double hook, the shaft turning with the fingers—the two men's methods were utterly opposed.

sentences.zh: 吳育，字山子，江蘇吳江人。

translations.literal: Wu Yu, style name Shanzi, a man of Wujiang in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yu, courtesy name Shanzi, was a native of Wujiang in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 與包世臣、李兆洛遊，能文，工書。

translations.literal: He associated with Bao Shichen and Li Zhaoluo, was able in letters, and skilled in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: He associated with Bao Shichen and Li Zhaoluo, wrote well, and was accomplished in calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 謂：「下筆須使筆毫平鋪紙上，乃四面圓足，此陽冰篆法，書家真秘密語。」

translations.literal: He said: 'In setting down the brush one must make the hairs lie flat on the paper so that all four sides are rounded and full—this is Yangbing's seal method, the calligrapher's true secret words.'
translations.idiomatic: He said, 'When you set down the brush the hairs must lie flat on the paper so that all four sides are rounded and full—this is Li Yangbing's seal-script secret, the calligrapher's true inner teaching.'

sentences.zh: 世臣取其說。

translations.literal: Shichen adopted his doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Shichen adopted this doctrine.

sentences.zh: 育篆書尤工，法與石如差近。

translations.literal: Yu was especially skilled in seal script; his method differed little from Shiru's.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yu was especially accomplished in seal script, his manner close to Shiru's.

sentences.zh: 楊沂孫，字詠春，江蘇常熟人。

translations.literal: Yang Yisun, style name Yongchun, a man of Changshu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yisun, courtesy name Yongchun, was a native of Changshu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光二十三年舉人，官安徽鳳陽知府。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Daoguang he became a provincial graduate and served as prefect of Fengyang in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the twenty-third year of Daoguang and served as prefect of Fengyang in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸，遂不出，自號濠叟，少學於李兆洛，治週、秦諸子。

translations.literal: On returning for his father's mourning he did not emerge again, styled himself Haosou, studied under Li Zhaoluo in youth, and worked on the Zhou and Qin masters.
translations.idiomatic: After retiring for his father's mourning he never returned to office, took the sobriquet Haosou, studied under Li Zhaoluo in his youth, and devoted himself to the Zhou and Qin philosophers.

sentences.zh: 耽書法，尤致力於篆、籀，著文字解說問譌，欲補苴段玉裁、王筠所未備。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to calligraphy, especially to seal and zhou scripts, authored Corrections to Explanations of Characters, wishing to supplement what Duan Yucai and Wang Yun had not provided.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to calligraphy, above all seal and large-seal script, and wrote Corrections to Explanations of Characters, seeking to fill gaps left by Duan Yucai and Wang Yun.

sentences.zh: 又考上古逮史籀、李斯，折衷於許慎，作在昔篇。

translations.literal: He also examined antiquity down through Shi Zhou and Li Si, reconciling them through Xu Shen, and wrote the Zaixi Pian.
translations.idiomatic: He also traced writing from high antiquity through Shi Zhou and Li Si, reconciling them with Xu Shen's tradition, and composed the Zaixi Pian.

sentences.zh: 篆、隸宗石如，而多自得。

translations.literal: In seal and clerical script he took Shiru as patriarch yet had much of his own attainment.
translations.idiomatic: In seal and clerical script he followed Shiru yet achieved much on his own.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「吾書篆、籀，頡頏鄧氏，得意處或過之；

translations.literal: He once said: 'In my seal and zhou script I rival the Deng house, and in inspired passages may surpass it;
translations.idiomatic: He once said, 'In seal and large-seal script I can match the Deng school, and in my best passages may even surpass it;

sentences.zh: 分、隸則不能及也。」

translations.literal: in clerical script I cannot reach it.'
translations.idiomatic: but in clerical script I cannot equal him.'

sentences.zh: 光緒七年，卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Guangxu he died at sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of Guangxu at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 沂孫同時工篆、籀者，又推吳大澂，自有傳。

translations.literal: Among those of Yisun's time skilled in seal and zhou script, Wu Dacheng was also esteemed and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Among contemporaries skilled in seal and large-seal script, Wu Dacheng was also highly regarded and has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 吳熙載，初名廷颺，以字行，後又字讓之，江蘇儀徵人。

translations.literal: Wu Xizai, original name Tingyang, went by his style name, later also styled Rangzhi, a man of Yizheng in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xizai, originally named Tingyang, went by his style name and later also took the style Rangzhi; he came from Yizheng in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 先世居江寧，父明煌，始遊揚州，善相人術。

translations.literal: His forebears lived in Jiangning; his father Minghuang first traveled to Yangzhou and was skilled in physiognomy.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long lived in Jiangning; his father Minghuang first traveled to Yangzhou and was skilled in physiognomy.

sentences.zh: 熙載為諸生，博學多能，從包世臣學書。

translations.literal: Xizai was a licentiate, broadly learned and multi-talented, and studied calligraphy under Bao Shichen.
translations.idiomatic: Xizai was a licentiate, broadly learned and accomplished in many arts, and studied calligraphy under Bao Shichen.

sentences.zh: 世臣創明北朝書派，溯源窮流，為一家之學。

translations.literal: Shichen elucidated the Northern Dynasties calligraphic school, tracing sources and exhausting currents, forming a school of his own.
translations.idiomatic: Shichen clarified the Northern Dynasties calligraphic school, tracing its sources to their limits and founding a school of his own.

sentences.zh: 其筆法兼採同時黃乙生、王良士、吳育、硃昂之、鄧石如諸人之說。

translations.literal: His brush method combined the doctrines of his contemporaries Huang Yisheng, Wang Liangshi, Wu Yu, Zhu Angzhi, Deng Shiru, and others.
translations.idiomatic: His brush method drew on the teachings of his contemporaries Huang Yisheng, Wang Liangshi, Wu Yu, Zhu Angzhi, Deng Shiru, and others.

sentences.zh: 執筆，食指高鉤，大指加食指、中指之間，中指內鉤，小指貼名指外拒，管向左迤，後稍偃，若指鼻準。

translations.literal: In holding the brush the forefinger hooked high, the thumb placed between forefinger and middle finger, the middle finger hooked inward, the little finger pressed against the ring finger outward in resistance, the shaft slanting left, then slightly tilted back as if pointing at the nose.
translations.idiomatic: He held the brush with the forefinger hooked high, the thumb between forefinger and middle finger, the middle finger hooked inward, the little finger braced against the ring finger, the shaft angled left and then tilted slightly back as if pointing at the nose.

sentences.zh: 運鋒，使筆毫平鋪紙上，筆筆斷而後起。

translations.literal: In moving the tip he made the hairs lie flat on the paper; each stroke broke off and then rose again.
translations.idiomatic: In moving the tip he spread the hairs flat on the paper, each stroke lifting only after a distinct break.

sentences.zh: 結字計白當黑，使左右牝牡相得，自謂合古人八法、九宮之旨。

translations.literal: In structuring characters he balanced white against black, making left and right male and female correspond, and said of himself that this accorded with the ancients' Eight Methods and Nine Palaces.
translations.idiomatic: In structuring characters he balanced white space against ink, pairing complementary forms left and right, and held that this fulfilled the ancients' Eight Methods and Nine Palaces.

sentences.zh: 熙載恪守師法，世臣真、行、藁草無不工，嗜篆、分而未致力，熙載篆、分功力尤深。

translations.literal: Xizai strictly observed his teacher's method; Shichen was skilled in regular, running, and draft-cursive alike, loved seal and clerical script but had not devoted himself to them—Xizai's seal and clerical power was especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: Xizai adhered strictly to his teacher's method; Shichen excelled in regular, running, and draft-cursive script but, though fond of seal and clerical script, had not devoted himself to them—whereas Xizai's mastery of seal and clerical script was especially profound.

sentences.zh: 复縱筆作畫，亦有士氣。

translations.literal: He also freely wielded the brush in painting, which likewise had scholarly air.
translations.idiomatic: He also painted freely with the brush, and his paintings likewise had a literati air.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，卒。

translations.literal: In the Xianfeng reign he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Xianfeng reign.

sentences.zh: 與熙載同受包氏法者，江都梅植之蘊生，甘泉楊亮季子，高涼黃洵修存，餘姚毛長齡仰蘇，旌德姚配中仲虞，松桃楊承汪挹之。

translations.literal: Those who like Xizai received the Bao school's method included Mei Zhizhi Yunsheng of Jiangdu, Yang Liang Jizi of Ganquan, Huang Xun Xiucun of Gaoliang, Mao Changling Yangsu of Yuyao, Yao Peizhong Zhongyu of Jingde, and Yang Chengwang Yizhi of Songtao.
translations.idiomatic: Others who studied under the Bao school alongside Xizai included Mei Zhizhi Yunsheng of Jiangdu, Yang Liang Jizi of Ganquan, Huang Xun Xiucun of Gaoliang, Mao Changling Yangsu of Yuyao, Yao Peizhong Zhongyu of Jingde, and Yang Chengwang Yizhi of Songtao.

sentences.zh: 配中詳儒林傳。

translations.literal: Peizhong is treated in detail in the Biographies of Confucian Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Peizhong is treated at length in the Biographies of Confucian Scholars.

sentences.zh: 植之，道光十九年舉人。

translations.literal: Zhizhi became a provincial graduate in the nineteenth year of Daoguang.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Zhizhi passed the provincial examination in the nineteenth year of Daoguang.

sentences.zh: 通經，以詩鳴，世臣尤稱其書。

translations.literal: He mastered the classics, was famed for poetry, and Shichen especially praised his calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in the classics, won fame as a poet, and Shichen especially praised his calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 謂其跌宕遒麗，段煉舊搨，血脈精氣，奔赴腕下，熙載未之敢先。

translations.literal: He said it was free and bold, vigorous and beautiful, segment by segment refining old rubbings, blood and breath and vital essence rushing to the wrist—Xizai did not dare rank before him.
translations.idiomatic: He called it bold and graceful, refined stroke by stroke from old rubbings, with vital energy pouring through the wrist—Xizai himself did not dare claim precedence.

sentences.zh: 又得琴法於吳思伯之女弟子顏夫人，獨具神解。

translations.literal: He also obtained qin method from Wu Sibo's female disciple Lady Yan, and had a unique spiritual understanding.
translations.idiomatic: He also learned the qin from Lady Yan, a female disciple of Wu Sibo, and attained a singular spiritual understanding of the instrument.

sentences.zh: 糾正思伯傳譜，於古操製曲之故，輒能知之。

translations.literal: Correcting Sibo's transmitted scores, he could always know the reasons behind ancient pieces and how melodies were composed.
translations.idiomatic: Correcting Sibo's transmitted scores, he could explain the origins of ancient pieces and how they were composed.

sentences.zh: 自署所居曰嵇庵。

translations.literal: He styled his dwelling Ji Hermitage.
translations.idiomatic: He named his residence the Ji Hermitage.

sentences.zh: 配中與有同嗜，著琴學二卷。

translations.literal: Peizhong shared the same passion and authored two juan of Qin Studies.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Peizhong shared his passion and wrote two fascicles of Qin Studies.

sentences.zh: 植之五十而卒，琴法未有傳書。

translations.literal: Zhizhi died at fifty; his qin method had no transmitted book.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Zhizhi died at fifty, and his qin method was never set down in writing.

sentences.zh: 亮，世為將家，襲騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: Liang came from a military family for generations and inherited the hereditary post of Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Liang came from a long line of military families and inherited the hereditary post of Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 篤學敦行，江、淮間士大夫多稱之。

translations.literal: He studied earnestly and conducted himself sincerely; gentry between the Yangtze and Huai often praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply learned and upright in conduct, and literati between the Yangtze and Huai spoke highly of him.

sentences.zh: 書亞於熙載。

translations.literal: His calligraphy ranked below Xizai's.
translations.idiomatic: His calligraphy ranked just below Xizai's.

sentences.zh: 合肥沈用熙最後出，至光緒末始卒，年近八十。

translations.literal: Shen Yongxi of Hefei appeared last; he did not die until the end of Guangxu, nearly eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yongxi of Hefei was the latest of the group; he did not die until the end of the Guangxu reign, at nearly eighty.

sentences.zh: 畢生守師法，最為包門老弟子。

translations.literal: He kept the teacher's method all his life and was the oldest disciple of the Bao school.
translations.idiomatic: He observed his teacher's method to the end of his life and was the senior surviving disciple of the Bao school.

sentences.zh: 世臣敘次清一代書人為五品，分九等：「平和簡靜，遒麗天成，曰神品；

translations.literal: Shichen arranged Qing calligraphers in five grades divided into nine ranks: 'Even, peaceful, simple, and still; forceful and beautiful, heaven-born—this is the divine grade;
translations.idiomatic: Shichen ranked Qing calligraphers in five grades subdivided into nine ranks: 'Even, peaceful, simple, and still; forceful and beautiful as if heaven-made—this is the divine grade;

sentences.zh: 醖釀無跡，橫直相安，曰妙品；

translations.literal: brewed without trace, horizontal and vertical at peace—this is the marvelous grade;
translations.idiomatic: brewed without visible effort, horizontal and vertical strokes at peace—this is the marvelous grade;

sentences.zh: 逐跡尋源，思力交至，曰能品；

translations.literal: following traces to seek sources, thought and force arriving together—this is the capable grade;
translations.idiomatic: tracing forms back to their sources with thought and force united—this is the capable grade;

sentences.zh: 楚調自歌，不謬風雅，曰逸品；

translations.literal: Chu tunes sung to oneself, not straying from the Airs and Elegances—this is the transcendent grade;
translations.idiomatic: singing Chu airs in one's own voice without betraying the classical tradition—this is the transcendent grade;

sentences.zh: 墨守跡象，雅有門庭，曰佳品。

translations.literal: ink guarding traces and forms, elegantly having a school gate—this is the fine grade.
translations.idiomatic: clinging to outward forms yet maintaining a distinct school—this is the fine grade.

sentences.zh: 神品一人，鄧石如隸及篆書。

translations.literal: Divine grade, one person: Deng Shiru in clerical and seal script.
translations.idiomatic: Divine grade, one artist: Deng Shiru in clerical and seal script.

sentences.zh: 妙品上一人，鄧石如分及真書；

translations.literal: Marvelous grade, upper rank, one person: Deng Shiru in clerical division and regular script;
translations.idiomatic: Marvelous grade, upper rank, one artist: Deng Shiru in clerical and regular script;

sentences.zh: 妙品下二人，劉墉小真書，姚鼐行草書。

translations.literal: marvelous grade, lower rank, two people: Liu Yong in small regular script, Yao Nai in running-cursive script.
translations.idiomatic: marvelous grade, lower rank, two artists: Liu Yong in small regular script and Yao Nai in running-cursive script.

sentences.zh: 能品上七人，釋邱山真及行書，宋玨分榜書，傅山草書，姜宸英行書，鄧石如草書，劉墉榜書，黃乙生行榜書；

sentences.zh: 其後包氏之學盛行，咸、同以來，以書名者，何紹基、張裕釗、翁同龢三家最著，並見他傳。

translations.literal: Afterward the Bao school's learning flourished; from the Xianfeng and Tongzhi reigns onward, those famous for calligraphy were most renowned in the three houses of He Shaoji, Zhang Yuzhao, and Weng Tonghe—all are seen in other biographies.

sentences.zh: 紹基宗顏平原法，晚復出入漢分；

translations.literal: Shaoji took Yan Pingyuan's method as patriarch and in his later years again moved in and out of Han clerical script;

sentences.zh: 裕釗源出於包氏；

translations.literal: Yuzhao's source came from the Bao house;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuzhao's lineage came from the Bao school;

sentences.zh: 同龢規模閎變，不為諸家所囿，為一代後勁雲。

translations.literal: Tonghe's scope was vast and transforming, not confined by the various schools, and he was the sustaining force of a generation.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Tonghe worked on a grand and ever-changing scale, unbound by earlier schools, and stood as the great sustaining force of his generation.
